sobremesa--brulee.description: A 2019 reworking of Sobremesa made at Joya de Nicaragua, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper over a Mexican San Andrés binder; the Pennsylvania ligero is gone and more Condega seco added. Smooth and buttery, with cream, toast, coffee and nuts, and more depth than most Connecticut cigars.

thirds.notes: Sweet cream and butter lead, with toast, coffee, a nutty touch and a little white pepper.
The cream recedes; toast and coffee move forward, earth grows and pepper picks up on the retrohale.
Earth and coffee stay in front as the pepper peaks, with only a trace of sweetness left.

sobremesa--sobremesa-original.description: Steve Saka's first Dunbarton blend, released in 2015 and made at Joya de Nicaragua: a La Meca Ecuadorian Habano Rosado wrapper and Mexican Matacapan binder around four Nicaraguan fillers and Pennsylvania Broadleaf ligero. A rich, balanced after-dinner cigar of cocoa, earth and cedar with a creamy middle.

thirds.notes: Cocoa and earth lead over cedar and espresso, with black pepper on the retrohale and a hint of citrus.
The texture turns creamy around chocolate and earth, with nuts and a gentle, lingering spice.
Cedar and earth come forward, the cream fades, and dark chocolate and nuts stay to the end.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Sobremesa Cervantes Fino review

sobremesa--solita.description: Sobremesa Solita carries the original Sobremesa blend: a La Meca Ecuadorian Habano #1 Rosado wrapper, Mexican Matacapan binder and Nicaraguan fillers with Pennsylvania Broadleaf ligero, in four sizes. It smokes deep and earthy, with cocoa, cedar and coffee and a long, spiced finish.

sources.title: Luxury Cigar Club – Dunbarton Sobremesa Solita
